question: Client assets per advisor across the five -- and is that comparison even valid?

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: The 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 26, 2026, published October 14, 2026) states that Total Client Assets reached $10.5 trillion, with CFO Sharon Yeshaya saying, "With $10.5 trillion in total client assets across Wealth and Investment Management, we have the foundation to build on as we close out the year." The firm defines Total Client Assets as the sum of the reported Wealth Management client assets and Investment Management AUM, per the strategic update deck.
The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 3Q26 press release (period ended September 30, 2026) states total client assets were $13.33 trillion, up 15% year-over-year.

Edward Jones: The fiscal year 2025 10-K states the Partnership ended the year with a 14% increase in client assets under care (AUC) to $2.5 trillion, including $1.1 trillion of advisory programs AUC. The 2Q26 10-Q states the Partnership ended the second quarter of 2026 with $2.6 trillion of assets under care, including $1.2 trillion of advisory programs AUC.

Merrill: The 3Q26 GWIM press release (period ended September 30, 2026) states Merrill Wealth Management reported $1.9 trillion in AUM balances. Merrill's AUM is defined as managed assets under advisory and/or discretion of GWIM.

Raymond James Financial: The 2Q26 supplement (period ended June 30, 2026) reports client assets under administration of $1,922.4 billion as of June 30, 2026 (and $1,762.9 billion as of March 31, 2026, and $1,773.1 billion as of December 31, 2025).

Morgan Stanley: The 4Q20 supplement (period ended December 31, 2020) reports 15,950 Wealth Management representatives as of December 31, 2020, with 15,469 as of September 30, 2020, and 15,468 as of December 31, 2019.

Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q reports 20,514 financial advisors (actual) at period end for the second quarter of 2026, and an average of 20,537 for the same quarter; the fiscal year 2025 10-K reports 20,425 financial advisors (actual) at year end 2025.

Raymond James Financial: Whole firm basis — the fiscal 2025 10-K reports total financial advisors of 8,943 as of September 30, 2025 (3,878 employee and 5,065 independent contractor), 8,787 as of September 30, 2024, and 8,712 as of September 30, 2023. Private Client Group basis — the 2025 investor day deck reports 8,731 PCG advisors as of approximately March 31, 2025. These are different bases and are not one series.

Whether client assets per advisor across the five firms can be validly compared side by side: No, the comparison is not valid on this evidence. The five firms do not measure client assets or advisor headcount on the same basis, and the ratio is unverified (not in the metric definitions file). The client asset measures differ: Morgan Stanley reports Total Client Assets (the sum of Wealth Management client assets and Investment Management AUM) and, separately, advisor-led client assets (assets in accounts with a Wealth Management representative assigned, a subset of total client assets); Schwab reports total client assets split between an Investor Services retail segment and an Advisor Services segment that acts as custodian for independent RIAs (more than 16,000 advisory firms) rather than a count of Schwab's own financial advisors; Edward Jones reports client assets under care ('AUC'); Merrill reports AUM (managed assets under advisory and/or discretion of GWIM) and total client balances; and Raymond James reports client assets under administration (AUA), with advisor counts that exclude advisors in its RCS division even though their client assets are included in AUA. The advisor-count measures differ likewise: Morgan Stanley counts 'Wealth Management representatives' (latest figure 15,950 as of December 31, 2020); Schwab publishes no advisor headcount, only Form ADV employee counts; Edward Jones counts 'financial advisors' on an actual headcount basis; Merrill's 'total wealth advisors' figure includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking (broader than Merrill alone); and Raymond James counts employee and independent contractor financial advisors while excluding RCS advisors. Because these definitions, scopes, units (AUM vs. AUC vs. AUA; representatives vs. advisors vs. firms), and periods differ across firms, and the per-advisor ratio itself is unverified, the figures cannot be validly compared side by side.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: The 3Q26 supplement (period ended September 30, 2026) reports total Wealth Management client assets of $8,433 billion, and advisor-led client assets (assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned) of $6,631 billion; the 4Q25 supplement reports fee-based client assets as 48% of advisor-led client assets at year-end 2025. The firm's most recent advisor-count disclosure is 15,950 Wealth Management representatives as of December 31, 2020.
adjacent.differs_because: These are total Wealth Management client assets and advisor-led client assets, not a computed client-assets-per-advisor figure; the firm does not disclose a current advisor headcount to pair with them.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 3Q26 press release reports Advisor Services segment client assets of $5,845.9 billion as of September 30, 2026; the 3Q26 earnings call reports Schwab serves more than 16,000 advisory firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets; Schwab publishes no financial-advisor headcount, only Form ADV employee counts (approximately 4,127 employees perform investment advisory functions including research).
adjacent.differs_because: These are custodial assets of independent advisory firms and firm/employee counts, not Schwab's own client assets per financial advisor; Schwab reports advisor-side activity as independent RIAs rather than individual advisors.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones: For fiscal year 2025, the Partnership ended with $2.5 trillion in client assets under care and 20,425 financial advisors; for the second quarter of 2026, it ended with 20,514 financial advisors and (per the 2Q26 statement) $2.6 trillion in client assets under care as of June 26, 2026.
adjacent.differs_because: The numerator (client assets under care) and denominator (financial advisors) are disclosed separately; Edward Jones does not disclose a computed client-assets-per-advisor figure.

adjacent.text: Merrill: The 3Q26 supplement (period ended September 30, 2026) reports Merrill Wealth Management client balances of $4,240,601 million; the investor day deck reports Merrill and the Private Bank together have more than 15,000 wealth advisors, and the 4Q23 supplement reports 18,916 total wealth advisors including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.
adjacent.differs_because: These are client balances and a broader wealth-advisor count (Merrill plus Private Bank, or all GWIM and Consumer Banking wealth businesses), not a Merrill-only client-assets-per-advisor figure.

adjacent.text: Raymond James Financial: The fiscal 2025 10-K reports Private Client Group client assets under administration of $1.67 trillion (of which $1.01 trillion in fee-based accounts) and 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025; the Financial Institutions Division reports $166 million in average assets under management per advisor across 940 advisors at 160 financial institutions (undated web page, page content as of May 17, 2026).
adjacent.differs_because: The PCG AUA and advisor count are disclosed separately rather than as a per-advisor ratio, and the $166 million per-advisor figure is specific to the Financial Institutions Division, not the firm as a whole.

gaps.what: The Charles Schwab Corporation — advisor headcount: Schwab publishes no single 'advisor headcount' for the firm; the passages give only Form ADV employee counts (investment advisory functions, IARs, total employees) and full-time-equivalent employee counts, none of which equals a count of Schwab's own financial consultants and wealth advisors.

Merrill — advisor headcount: Merrill does not publish a Merrill-only advisor headcount; the disclosed 'total wealth advisors' figure includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking, and the >15,000 wealth advisors figure is for Merrill combined with the Private Bank.
gaps.suggested_source: BAC supplement (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2) and investor day deck (BAC-DECK-2025-investor-day#9)
